title: A Double Quote Inside Single Quotes

learning.python:
You've put a single quote inside a double-quoted string, and written a string between single quotes (see Learned earlier at the bottom of this page). The two fit together: a double quote, ", can go inside a single-quoted string just as it is:

print('She said "hi".')   # prints: She said "hi".

A single-quoted string ends at its closing ', so a " inside it is just another character.

You may also see \", a backslash before the quote. Inside single quotes it prints the same ", but it isn't needed there.
